## What's new

Threadnote 5.1.1 gives Manager a clearer workspace for writing memories, resolving decisions and sharing conflicts, managing Obsidian, and keeping the runtime up to date.

### A consistent Manager workspace

- Navigate every module through a shared sidebar, icons, and header breadcrumbs. Collapse the sidebar when you need more room, and keep your Light, Dark, or System appearance choice across sessions.
- Read graph views with clearer light-mode contrast, a stable canvas height, and a scrollable inspector. Processes and Runtime Health use descriptive rows and distinct status labels.

### Write and organize memories

- Create a memory directly from Home or Library with a rich Markdown editor, formatting controls, syntax-highlighted code, and Markdown source editing.
- Library keeps Memories and Resources together while making local memories and individual teams easier to select.
- Selecting a folder includes its collapsed and filtered descendants. Bulk actions and item menus let you archive, publish, unpublish, or forget the intended memories; removing a memory folder also forgets its contents.
- Resize the Library navigator to suit your workspace. Long names truncate with an ellipsis while keeping selection controls and item menus available.

### Resolve decisions and sharing conflicts

- Context Health opens review and task dialogs with the relevant case and evidence. Grouped cases expose every affected memory, and Home includes retained decisions that still need attention.
- Sharing compares local and shared versions, shows their differences, and lets you keep either version or save a manual resolution. Revision checks protect against resolving a conflict whose contents changed while you were reviewing it.
- Sidebar badges show shared conflicts and memories needing attention, with meaningful status colors in Context Health.

### Manage integrations and updates

- The new Integrations section manages Obsidian sources, selected memory exports, connection settings, and Inbox review candidates. Imports retain a preview-and-apply workflow; exports run directly and show their results. Existing vault edits and unmanaged notes remain protected.
- Runtime Health now includes an automatic-update toggle, an explicit update check, release notes for the installed and available versions, and an Update Threadnote action with progress and restart guidance.

### More reliable context recall

- Recall and Context Brief from a repository now keep unrelated projects' private memories out of results while retaining projectless guidance and intentionally selected worksets.
- Default recall can show a semantically strong match that falls just below the topical score cutoff, with its low confidence clearly labeled. An explicitly configured threshold remains strict.

MCP validation errors also identify an invalid `replaceUri` correctly, making memory replacement mistakes easier to fix.
